summary.headline: RPG Life Sciences Q2 FY27 revenue rose 16.5% to INR 211.6 crores and adjusted EBITDA rose 15% to INR 50.1 crores, with API acquisitions closing late September.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was the first quarter above INR 200 crores revenue and INR 50 crores EBITDA, with all three businesses growing. Adjusted EBITDA excluded INR 5.5 crores of one-time restructuring and API acquisition costs; gross margin expanded 260 bps despite West Asia-related input and freight pressure. Domestic formulations slowed to 11.6% growth, which management attributed to a planned inventory reduction (42 to 38 days) and a third-party supply disruption now resolved in October. The acquired API sites (Actis, Raghava) contributed only INR 0.5 crore in Q2, with billing starting Q3.

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted EBITDA (Q2, excl. INR 5.5 crores one-offs)

segments.name: Domestic formulations (~70% of revenue)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 145.7 crores, +11.6% YoY; H1 INR 278 crores, +13%. H1 volume growth 6.8% vs market 3.4%. Management said growth would have been 15.2% excluding the inventory reduction and supply disruption.

segments.name: International formulations
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 36.7 crores, +6.4% YoY; H1 INR 71.7 crores, +7%. Management guided to double-digit growth from H2 FY27, citing new tenders won and CDMO projects.

segments.name: API (RPG Active Pharma)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 27.5 crores, +85.5% YoY; H1 INR 54.1 crores, +57.1%. Management said this growth was entirely organic. Q2 EBITDA margin not disclosed; H2 margin guided to mid-20s; H2 revenue guided at INR 25-30 crores from acquired assets.

guidance_outlook: Domestic formulations: management expects to return to above 1.5x market growth from Q3; Q3 outlook described as positive.
International formulations: double-digit growth expected from H2 FY27; Naprosyn Canada shipments to start mid-December 2026, with 25-30% initial market share targeted.

API: organic growth guided at double digits; company-wide API ambition of 25%+ CAGR over 5 years; at least 30% CAGR over 3-5 years implies INR 300-350 crores by FY30 and INR 500 crores by FY32, subject to further acquisitions.
Margins: management aspires to reach FY25 EBITDA margin of about 24.5% and said H1 FY27 margin of 24% is close; some near-term margin compromise possible from growth investments.
Capex: no change to planned capex apart from acquired assets; capex expected below 7-8% of sales.
Cash flow: management declined to give a timeline for cash flow normalisation; to revisit after Q3 and Q4 once acquired sites stabilise.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing footprint expanded from 3 to 5 sites (2 formulation, 3 API) with the Actis and Raghava acquisitions, at Navi Mumbai, Visakhapatnam and Kamareddy near Hyderabad.
Post-acquisition API network: 5x manufacturing capacity, 4x reactors, 3x product and pipeline molecules, 2x customers and employees (management comparison).
Raghava plant ramp-up has started; Actis has a strong order book.
Some capex expected at acquired sites during integration; amount not quantified.
demand_pricing: Domestic formulations: Pharmarack covered market about INR 49,600 crores, growing 9.8% in H1. RPG ranked 50th (from 62nd in March 2025) and is the fourth-fastest-growing company on a MAT basis.
Q2 growth by basket: MAB +24%, nephrology and rheumatology +23%, cardio +18%, immunosuppressants +13%.
Naprosyn crossed INR 100 crores secondary sales on MAT basis; H1 primary sales INR 47.9 crores (+13.6%). Secondary growth about 14%.
Field productivity (PCPM) rose from INR 6.5 lakh to INR 7.17 lakh.
Pricing: price increases taken to pass through West Asia-related cost increases; trade discounts rationalised and returns reduced.
Launches from FY26 (12 brands) delivered INR 12.4 crores in H1 vs INR 6.3 crores last year; Norpace grew 40% in H1.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify acquired API revenue and EBITDA for FY27, and steady-state working capital and cash conversion.
qa_highlights.answer: EBITDA margin guided to mid-20s, in line with existing API business; H2 top line INR 25-30 crores. Cash flow generation too early to guide because integration is under way and some capex is expected; to revisit after Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 260 bps gross margin expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases, product mix across all three segments, company-level cost initiatives, a planned strategic inventory build, and a small FX tailwind, which offset West Asia war costs. Also converting some customers from CIF to ex-works terms.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee costs grow faster than revenue, and will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Conversion of contract labour to fixed employees and FY27 field-force additions after a Q3-Q4 FY26 headcount freeze. Management said the cost level is now normal and hiring is largely complete; output expected from H2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses grow faster than revenue, excluding the INR 5.5 crore one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly freight (export, import and domestic) linked to West Asia conflict and crude/diesel prices; the gap is about INR 7 crores, of which INR 5.5 crores is strategic initiatives. Normalisation depends on the conflict.

qa_highlights.question: Why did domestic formulations growth slow to 11.6% from 15-18% in prior quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory days cut from 42 to about 38 for hygiene (about INR 5-5.5 crores impact), plus a third-party manufacturer supply disruption in September, now resolved in October. Ex these factors, growth would have been 15.2%; Q3 outlook positive.

qa_highlights.question: Does management still target 1.5x market growth in domestic formulations, and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; expects to exceed 1.5x in coming quarters. Drivers: FY26 launches (about 50% of plan), three new molecules (Naprosyn ES at INR 3 crores so far, Critipenem, Flowaxis device), divisionalisation (cardiology +18%), and medical marketing.

qa_highlights.question: When will international formulations return to double-digit growth, and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Double-digit growth expected from H2 FY27; foray into 13 new markets, three R&D partnerships for MAs and dossiers, and 2 tenders already won. CDMO projects completed on time, with three more products in development.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for organic API growth and acquired business?
qa_highlights.answer: Organic API expected to grow at double digits. Order pipeline for Actis and Raghava stronger than expected, with no change to the outlook from the last call.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path back to FY25's 24.5% EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY25 level of 25% is the aspiration; H1 FY27 margin of 24% is close, and growth investments may compress margin slightly in the near term.

qa_highlights.question: Is capex at 7-8% of sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed capex below 7-8% of sales, with no change to planned capex apart from acquired-asset requirements.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict: continued freight and input cost pressure; management said freight normalisation depends on crude and diesel prices.
Domestic formulation growth durability after the Q2 slowdown; watch whether Q3 returns to above 1.5x market growth as guided.
Working capital and cash conversion: H2 cash flow was weak, and management gave no steady-state guidance.
Integration risk at Actis and Raghava; acquired API EBITDA margin only guided to mid-20s, and no Q2 API margin was disclosed.
Pharmarack vs reported DF growth gap, explained by PTR-level data and inventory changes; the bridge is qualitative.
Possible regulation of trade margins for oncology drugs (Supreme Court case); management said selling prices to distributors would be broadly unchanged, but MRP would fall.
Naprosyn Canada launch in mid-December 2026; first OTC product in the global market for the company, with 25-30% share targeted.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and strategy, with clear explanations of the Q2 domestic slowdown and margin levers. Cautious on cash flow and freight costs, where management declined to give timelines and tied outcomes to the West Asia conflict.
key_quotes: For the first time, we crossed INR 200 crores in quarterly revenue and INR 50 crores in quarterly EBITDA. All 3 of our businesses grew.
The growth is almost entirely organic. The acquired sites contributed only INR50 lakhs in quarter 2 as the transaction closed mid-year in September.
So cash flow generation, it's too early because it's an integration right now is happening.
So we are at 24% EBITDA margin in H1. So we are not very far off, okay?

adds.what: Acquired API sites (Actis, Raghava) bringing footprint from 3 to 5 sites; post-acquisition API network 5x manufacturing capacity, 4x reactors
Raghava plant ramp-up started; acquired API billing starts Q3 with H2 FY27 top line guided at INR 25-30 crore

growth.why: Management guides H1-based growth to continue with DF returning above 1.5x market from Q3, international double-digit from H2 (Naprosyn Canada shipments mid-December), and acquired API H2 revenue of INR 25-30 crore; backing is partly specific (acquired sites, H2 API range, launches of INR 12.4 crore in H1) but DF recovery and international growth rely on demand and tenders without quantified order

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin expanded 260 bps YoY in Q2 and H1 adjusted EBITDA margin is 24.0%, close to management's 24.5% aspiration, though growth investments may compress margin slightly near term.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Actis and Raghava acquisitions already closed end-September; API billing starts Q3 and Raghava ramp-up has started, taking footprint from 3 to 5 sites and API capacity to 5x.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Domestic formulations H1 volume growth was 6.8% vs market 3.4%, with management expecting DF to return above 1.5x market from Q3, international double-digit from H2, and acquired API revenue of INR 25-30 crore in H2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said there is no change to planned capex beyond acquired-asset needs, with capex held below 7-8% of sales; no utilisation figure was disclosed, so no new capacity announcement is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is confident on DF returning above 1.5x market and on API ambition of 30% CAGR, but the call gave no quantified raise to FY27 guidance and the Q2 DF miss was partly explained away.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Freight and input costs tied to West Asia conflict remain unresolved, cash flow timeline was declined, and DF growth was 11.6% in Q2 versus the 15.2% management said it would have been underlying; Q3 must show above 1.5x market to confirm.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Naprosyn Canada shipments start mid-December 2026 with a 25-30% initial share target, and three new molecules (Naprosyn ES, Critipenem, Flowaxis device) are in the pipeline; FY26 launches delivered INR 12.4 crore in H1 vs INR 6.3 crore last year.

rows.label: Naprosyn Canada launch and international double-digit growth
rows.why: Canada shipments start mid-December 2026 and international growth was only 6.4% in Q2 (INR 36.7 crore), with management guiding double-digit growth from H2 on 13 new markets and 2 tenders won.

rows.label: Price increases to pass through West Asia costs
rows.why: Price increases were taken to offset West Asia-related cost increases, and this, plus mix and cost initiatives, drove the 260 bps gross margin expansion in Q2.

tone.note: Management was confident on DF recovery above 1.5x market, API growth and launches, and cautious on cash flow timelines and West Asia freight; analysts pushed on the Q2 DF slowdown, employee and freight cost growth, and the path back to 24.5% margin.
